clue.text: Mark was first to be amused

parts.note: a tick is a mark made beside an item on a list
to have led a race is to have been first

explanation.surface: Someone notes that whoever made a mark first ended up entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tickled, in the figurative sense, is being delighted or entertained.

clue.text: Watch blood-sucking mite by eastern river

parts.note: a tick is a small blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A warning to look out for a parasite beside an eastern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' is a noun here, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a timepiece is called this because of the sound it makes; it also means the heart.

clue.text: Conservative politician surrounded by the man's creatures

indicators.note: the politician's letters are placed inside, with the other word around them

parts.note: his means belonging to the man
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Tory MP is hemmed in by some man's animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' signals the container; the Conservative abbreviation stands in front of it rather than inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these apes are a kind of animal, so living beings in general define them loosely.

clue.text: First vessel following the queen's command

indicators.note: the vessel comes after the other pieces

parts.note: to lead is to be in first place
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: The first ship to fall in behind the monarch's flagship takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being in command or charge of a group is having that role of guidance.

clue.text: Trade also includes business agreements

indicators.note: the two words hold the letters within them, across the word break

explanation.surface: Commerce involves contracts too.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'Trade' and the start of 'also'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: commercial bargains or transactions agreed between parties.

clue.text: Skilled Liberal Democrat keeping answer quiet

indicators.note: one name holds the other letters inside it, as if keeping them

parts.note: Vince Cable was a leader of the UK Liberal Democrats
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A talented Lib Dem politician keeps their reply to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals the container, the pair going in after the first letter. Vince Cable led Britain's Liberal Democrat party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone skilled at a task is competent and able to do it.

clue.text: Reptile picked up monster fish that is squeezing tail in channel

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word lifted upwards is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an orc is a monster from fantasy fiction
cod is a fish

indicators.note: the abbreviation holds a letter pressed inside it

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

indicators.note: the tail of the word channel is its last letter

explanation.surface: A reptile lifts a monstrous fish trapped in a channel by its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses the monster, as this is a down entry; 'squeezing' puts the channel's tail L into the Latin abbreviation, making ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this large-jawed river-dwelling creature is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Servant mellow under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, the mellow word sits below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to age is to mellow with time, like wine

explanation.surface: A household servant softens when placed under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts AGE beneath P in this down entry, giving P then AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a young attendant or footboy in a household or court is a kind of servant.

clue.text: Be purchasing correct clobber, finally getting smarter

indicators.note: buying something takes it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: right means correct

indicators.note: the final letter of clobber is taken

explanation.surface: Someone buying the right clothes ends up looking smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchasing' signals one word taken inside another, and 'finally' takes the last letter. Clobber is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone cleverer or more intelligent is brighter.

clue.text: Blokes cutting forged steel parts

indicators.note: the blokes word slices into the middle of the scrambled letters
metal that is forged is beaten into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: blokes are men

explanation.surface: Workmen cut parts out of steel in a forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges the metal word into ELETS, and 'cutting' splits that open to take the blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the components or constituents of a whole are its parts.

clue.text: Mate — a kind of tea

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang: ... plate stands for mate, a friend
a type of tea grown in that Asian country, as against Indian

explanation.surface: Someone offers a pal a particular variety of brew.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'china plate' (mate) to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming-slang word for a friend, and also the name of a tea type from the Far East.

clue.text: Next to a lengthy border

parts.note: something lengthy is long
the side of something is its edge or border

explanation.surface: Describes being positioned beside a long boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: to be next to something is to be beside it.

clue.text: Feeling fast current — no going back!

parts.note: an express train is a fast one
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: the word no is read backwards, as if travelling in reverse

explanation.surface: A sensation like a fast-flowing current from which there is no return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses the final word. I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: To play or sing with feeling is to do it with emotional colouring, as musicians put it.

clue.text: Heehaw, heehaw, showing indication of delight?

indicators.note: the letters are on show inside the repeated donkey noise, straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A donkey's braying is offered, tongue in cheek, as a sign of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of the first bray and the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation people shout on a fun ride to express glee, so a sign of pleasure.

clue.text: Having a rabbit worried the cat clique

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: a ring is a closed group or clique

explanation.surface: A cat is worried by a rabbit and a gang of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges THE CAT. 'Rabbit' is Cockney rhyming slang: rabbit and pork means talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: to rabbit, in British speech, is to talk on and on, which is gabbing incessantly.

clue.text: Doctor has ointments for shock

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician keeps creams to treat a patient in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb signalling the rearrangement of HAS OINTMENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shock and great surprise are the same reaction to something unexpected.

clue.text: Aida perhaps not about to retain international job

parts.note: Verdi's Aida is an example of an opera

indicators.note: the turned word keeps a letter inside it
the word not is turned round

explanation.surface: Perhaps Aida is not about to keep an international role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NOT to TON; 'to retain' puts I inside it, making TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a surgical procedure or a military undertaking is called a job in casual speech.

clue.text: Reshuffle so dire PM swore

indicators.note: a cabinet reshuffle rearranges ministers, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A desperate prime minister vowed to reorganise the cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reshuffle' rearranges SO DIRE PM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have given one's word or vowed is to have sworn.

clue.text: Animal gentleman captures right over lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits above the lake letter
the gentleman word takes a letter prisoner inside it

parts.note: a squire is a country gentleman

explanation.surface: A country gent catches a beast by the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' puts R inside SQUIRE; 'over' sets that above L in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this bushy-tailed tree-climbing rodent is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Emir enters, confused about queen's demands

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the queen abbreviation, as if placed about it
the letters of emir enters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled emir comes in and asks what a queen wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles EMIR ENTERS into RE-IREMENTS, and 'about' wraps that around QU.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: needs or necessities that someone insists on are their demands.

clue.text: Starts to experience complete terror after snake's appearance

indicators.note: the initial letters come after the snake word

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the starts of the three following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A snake appears and you begin to feel complete terror.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the look or outward aspect of something is how it appears.

clue.text: During forty winks it's still — or moving forty times

definitions.text: During forty winks it's still — or moving forty times

parts.words: During forty winks it's still — or moving forty times
parts.note: the body part described stays shut and motionless during a nap, or moves when you blink, and forty winks also suggests forty blinks

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that is motionless during a short sleep, or busy with forty movements.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty winks is a nap, but taken literally it is forty blinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the fold of skin over the eye stays closed when napping and flicks when winking.

clue.text: Male help? Female help!

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A query about help from a man, answered with an emphatic call for help from a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the contrast: M (male) plus AID (help) gives a female helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic servant who is a woman, such as a housemaid, is a female helper.

clue.text: Without thinking, really, chess moves husband's ignored

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, like pieces in a game
the husband letter is left out of the word chess

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone playing chess makes moves without thinking, really, ignoring their husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops H from CHESS to leave CESS; 'moves' then rearranges REALLY with CESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doing something heedlessly, without care or attention, is doing it without thinking.

clue.text: Editor, for example, turning up with small skirts

indicators.note: in a down clue the abbreviation is flipped upwards, reading bottom to top

explanation.surface: An editor, for example, arrives in small skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' flips EG to GE. 'skirts' is a verb here, not the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to skirt round something is to move along its borders, which is to edge around it.

clue.text: Every seaside place is topless

indicators.note: the seaside word loses its top, its first letter in a down entry

parts.note: a beach is a place at the seaside

explanation.surface: Every beach at the seaside allows topless bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is topless' removes the first letter B from BEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: every one of a group, taken one by one, is each of them.

clue.text: Rat swallowing dairy product, squealing

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside it, as if eating it

parts.note: to rat on someone is to inform, or sing, to the police
cream is a product of the dairy

explanation.surface: A rodent gulps down some cream and squeaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but is the verb for informing to the police; 'swallowing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: squealing and shrieking are both high-pitched cries.

clue.text: Perfect view by loch

parts.note: an idea is an opinion or view
L is a map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: A beautiful outlook beside a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something flawless, exactly as it should be, is perfect.

clue.text: One supposedly intelligent policeman unkindly rejected short clue

indicators.note: the word for the policeman is turned back to front, as if thrown back

parts.note: plod is a disparaging British slang word for a police officer

indicators.note: the word for clue is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: A clever officer is dismissed harshly for giving a brief tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns PLOD into DOLP; 'short' trims HINT to HIN. PLOD, from the children's character Mr Plod, is a mocking British name for police.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are widely regarded as among the cleverest animals, hence a famously smart creature.

clue.text: Observed insulted learner leaving

indicators.note: the learner letter departs from the word for insulted

parts.note: slighted means insulted
L is for learner, as on learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Someone saw a student storm off after being offended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes L out of SLIGHTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that has been spotted or seen has been observed.
